deep.reconstruction:
Context: §§1-3 of Grothendieck's 1974 'topologie modérée' notes. X is a topological space and F ⊂ P(X) is a family of subsets satisfying axioms a)-e) of §1. The axioms are not visible here; presumably they include closure under finite Boolean operations, closure and interior, and the requirement that boundaries of members are closed and nowhere dense ('rares'). On the previous page a finite 'décomposition cellulaire' is defined: a finite partition X = ⊔ X_i such that (1) the closure of each X_i is a union of pieces (frontier condition), and (2) distinct pieces have distinct closures. Grothendieck shows these are exactly the finite quotients φ: X → I = X/R that are T0 ('présobres') and for which φ is an open map. The specialisation order on I is then the incidence relation of the strata. A decomposition is F-admissible if all pieces lie in F.

This page states and begins proving the Proposition. Let L ⊂ F be finite. Then there is an F-admissible cellular decomposition of X such that every Y ∈ L is a union of pieces. Among all such decompositions there is a coarsest one, which is canonical.

Proof sketch, by dimension induction:
- Let X' = ⋃_{Y∈L} Ẏ, where Ẏ is the boundary (frontière) of Y. It is a finite union of closed nowhere-dense sets, hence closed and nowhere dense. Let U = X \ X', which is open and dense.
- Since U misses every ∂Y, each Y ∩ U is clopen in U.
- Take the coarsest finite partition (U_i) of U into atoms of the Boolean algebra generated by the Y ∩ U. Each U_i is a finite intersection of the Y ∩ U and their complements in U, hence clopen in U.
- Replace (X, L) by (X', L'), where L' = {Y ∩ X'} ∪ {cl(U_i) ∩ X'}.
- If (X'_j) is a decomposition of X' adapted to L', then {X'_j} ∪ {U_i} is one for X (finished on the next page). The cl(U_i) ∩ X' in L' ensure the frontier condition for the new open strata.
- Termination uses (Dim): a chain X_1 ⊃ X_2 ⊃ … of closed members of F, each nowhere dense in the previous one, is eventually empty.

Corollaries on the next page: (1) F is the filtered union of the Boolean algebras F_P generated by admissible decompositions; (2) the set of admissible decompositions, ordered by refinement, has suprema of finite subsets.

Modern reading: an axiomatic 'tame' version of the existence of a canonical coarsest stratification with frontier condition, compatible with finitely many definable sets. This is the analogue of o-minimal cell/stratification theorems. The previous page also encodes stratifications as open continuous maps to finite T0 spaces, i.e. finite posets.
errors: The atoms U_i are intersections of the sets Y∩U and their complements in U, not just 'une intersection (finie) de tels ensembles Y∩U'. The conclusion (U_i clopen in U) is unaffected.

That X' is nowhere dense, that X' and the members of L' lie in F, and that boundaries relative to X' are again nowhere dense all rely on the unseen axioms a)-e). The induction also needs (Dim), which is only introduced on the next page.

The page asserts that a coarsest decomposition exists but does not prove it. A proof works: if Y is a union of pieces of a frontier-condition partition, then cl(Y), cl(X\Y) and ∂Y are unions of pieces too. So any compatible decomposition refines the canonical one, by induction. This argument is not written out here.

ideas.what: Finite stratifications with frontier condition (strata determined by their closures) correspond to finite T0 quotients X→I for which the quotient map is open; the incidence relation of strata is the specialisation order.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification as a continuous (here open) map to a finite poset with the Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; made systematic in Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A (c.2012), and Ayala-Francis-Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (tame topology, 'dévissages'); no explicit statement known

ideas.what: Axiomatic existence of an F-admissible cellular decomposition adapted to finitely many sets in F, with a canonical coarsest one. Proved by cutting out the union of boundaries and inducting on a dimension axiom.
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition / canonical stratification theorem in o-minimal (tame) geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Łojasiewicz, Hironaka (semi-analytic/semialgebraic); van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn (o-minimal, 1984-86)
ideas.where_published: Programme only announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5; this proof not published

ideas.what: Dimension axiom (Dim): chains of closed admissible sets, each nowhere dense in the previous one, terminate. Used as the induction principle.
ideas.modern_name: Finite dimension axiom for tame/o-minimal structures

ideas.what: Corollary: F is the filtered union of the Boolean algebras of admissible decompositions, and admissible decompositions form a directed set under refinement with finite suprema.
ideas.modern_name: Directed system of stratifications; a tame family as a colimit of finite posets of strata

missed.claim: A purely topological, axiomatic (pre-o-minimal) proof that a 'tame' family F satisfying closure/boundary/dimension axioms admits, for any finite L ⊂ F, a canonical coarsest frontier-condition stratification compatible with L. It also proves that admissible stratifications form a directed set with suprema.
missed.quote: Parmi toutes ces décompositions cellulaires, il y en a une plus grossière
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck had, in 1974, an axiomatic core of what became o-minimal stratification theory, independent of any model-theoretic language. The canonical coarsest stratification relative to only the frontier condition is a clean statement seldom isolated in the o-minimal literature.

missed.claim: Stratifications are encoded as open quotient maps to finite T0 spaces (posets). The ambient tame family is then the filtered colimit of the finite Boolean algebras of these posets of strata.
missed.quote: les décompositions cellulaires (finies) de X correspondent aux espaces quotients finis de X qui sont présobres, et tels que X → X/R soit ouverte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the poset-stratified-space viewpoint (Lurie, Ayala-Francis-Tanaka, exit-path ∞-categories) in a tame setting, with openness as the frontier condition. A specialist might find the pro-finite-poset description of a tame structure suggestive.

deep.surprise_reason: These are solid unpublished details of Grothendieck's 1974 tame-topology programme, anticipating o-minimal stratification and poset-stratified spaces. The mathematics itself is fairly elementary and its main results were later established independently by others.
transcription_corrections: 'décomposition alleluia[?]' (twice) is almost certainly 'décomposition cellulaire' / 'décompositions cellulaires'.
'réunions de familles' is probably 'réunions de facettes' (or 'de cellules'); likewise the previous page's 'feuilles' is likely 'facettes'.
'(unique au quelque déterminée)' is uncertain; it seems to qualify the coarsest decomposition as uniquely or canonically determined.
'(comme ensembliste il est dit)' is probably '(comme il est bien connu)' or similar, with 'ensembliste' inserted.
In L', the second family is {cl(U_i) ∩ X'}_{i∈I} (the closures of the U_i, overlined).
